transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Crestview Head of AI), Mike Alvarez (Infra), Sanjay Patel (Security), Rita Owens (Platform)

Summary: short sync to scope a 4-week POC focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling. Goals: define success criteria (latency, cost, quality), gather traffic profile (QPS, concurrency, token distributions), agree on benchmark plan and timeline, surface security requirements.

Topics: workload sizing, QPS targets, p95 latency SLO, token distribution (input/output), concurrency, host vs dedicated, benchmarks, timeline and next steps

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro from redwood side  maya and diego here, we'll run through the POC plan, make sure we understand your traffic and success criteria.
[00:18] Laura: hi, thanks. Laura here. we want to validate cost and latency for our customer support summarization pipeline. this is, uh, high volume during business hours  roughly two big spikes so need to model that.
[00:32] Mike: mike  infra. main constraints are VPC peering, strict egress limits and we need to keep PII off shared logs, so private deployment or dedicated is likely.
[00:44] Diego: noted  good to clarify. question up front: do you have a current QPS/concurrency baseline we can use? even ballpark numbers are helpful.
[00:52] Laura: yeah, ballpark. baseline average QPS is around 45, peak QPS around 180 for 10-15 minute bursts during regional mornings. concurrency observed at the service level is about 60 concurrent conversations at peak, but downstream processing backs up sometimes.
[01:05] Maya: ok, good. can you break down the chat vs single-turn summarization? like % of multi-turn flows vs single-turn?
[01:12] Laura: roughly 70% single-turn summarization (user submits a support transcript, we return a concise summary), 30% multi-turn assistant flows used by agents for follow-ups  those multi-turn ones average 3 to 6 turns.
[01:24] Diego: and token sizes? input/output distributions? we often model using median and 90th percentiles.
[01:30] Laura: median input tokens ~60, 90th ~280 (some threads are long), median output tokens ~120, 90th ~520 for full thread summaries.
[01:41] Rita: also note we do attachments stripping before sending, but text length varies a lot.
[01:47] Sanjay: security note: we require SOC2, audit logs, SSO (SAML), and KMS integration for keys. can't allow raw transcripts to be stored in shared hosted logs for more than 7 days.
[01:59] Maya: understood; redwood offers dedicated pools + private with KMS and audit log options. we'll include the security pack in the docs.
[02:08] Diego: for modeling, we typically ask for a small traffic sample CSV with timestamp, request_type, input_tokens, output_tokens, success/failure, latencies. that lets us construct QPS profiles and concurrency simulation.
[02:21] Laura: we can provide that  we'll anonymize. expect two weeks of data.
[02:26] Maya: perfect. next, success criteria  what would signal a successful POC?
[02:31] Laura: p95 latency under 500ms for single-turn summaries, under 1s for multi-turn agent flows; quality parity with our current model (we'll provide eval prompts), and cost per 1k tokens reduction target of 20% vs current infra.
[02:44] Mike: and for infra we need to verify stable throughput under bursts  no request queueing beyond 5s and autoscaling ramp under 2 minutes.
[02:55] Diego: good, we'll aim to measure p50/p95/p99, plus tail latencies during bursts. we'll also measure token throughput and per-token compute.
[03:06] Maya: timeline thought  4-week POC: week 1 integration + baseline ingestion, week 2 benchmark runs (synthetic + replay), week 3 quality evaluation against your eval set, week 4 runbook, handoff and final report. does that align?
[03:21] Laura: yes that's fine. we may need an extra week if legal/security review drags.
[03:26] Sanjay: we'll start security questionnaire in parallel  please send it asap.
[03:30] Maya: will do. Diego, quick note on workload modeling: we typically model two modes  steady state and bursty traffic. steady QPS you gave ~45, peak bursts up to 180. we'll simulate bursts of 10-15 minutes at 180 QPS and check CPU/GPU utilization and queuing.
[03:45] Diego: on concurrency, for multi-turn flows we maintain KV cache per session which increases memory usage; when modeling concurrency we treat multi-turn sessions as longer-lived holds on a slot. for instance, 30 concurrent multi-turn sessions with avg length 4 turns will change memory/kv pressure vs 60 single-turn requests.
[04:01] Mike: question: what's your guidance on batching? we are sensitive to latency but would like cost savings.
[04:07] Diego: batching helps for throughput but can add latency. we can use small-continuous batching with a 10-20ms window and dynamic thresholds driven by SLO. for your p95 target we'd probably keep tight windows for single-turns and allow slightly larger windows during non-peak.
[04:22] Laura: ok. and model size  are you recommending quantized medium models or larger?
[04:28] Maya: depends on quality target. our recommendation: start with a 13B quantized variant to hit cost/latency targets; if quality gaps appear, test 33B or float32 on dedicated hardware. diego will propose a model matrix.
[04:41] Diego: yes i'll put together a shortlist: 7B/13B quantized candidates for cost tests, 33B for quality comparison. we'll include Redwood-verified throughput numbers per GPU type.
[04:50] Sanjay: for private deployment we will need to verify on-prem footprint: GPUs, network egress, and offline key management.
[04:58] Maya: noted  we'll include private deployment checklist in the security packet.
[05:03] Rita: regarding benchmarks, do you do both replay and synthetic workloads?
[05:07] Diego: yes, we do replay (your real traffic) and synthetic microbenchmarks to isolate model perf. replay helps validate token distributions and concurrency. synthetic helps isolate kernel/hotpath.
[05:18] Maya: also we'll run cost modeling  per-token CPU/GPU seconds and per-hour GPU cost to estimate $/1M tokens.
[05:25] Laura: please include a sensitivity analysis for token size  we are worried about tail conversations.
[05:30] Diego: we'll provide p50/p90/p95 token buckets and show how cost scales with tails. also suggest prefix/KV caching opportunities for repeated queries to reduce cost.
[05:41] Mike: on infra side, our VPC has strict egress windows and we use private endpoints  how do you handle peering?
[05:48] Maya: we have options: hosted with private networking (VPC peering) or dedicated with isolated GPU pools. we'll share network diagrams and expected ports.
[05:58] Laura: can you run an initial microbenchmark that simulates 100 QPS of 60-token inputs to give us a feel?
[06:05] Diego: yes  i can spin up a quick run using our harness; probably will run on a benchmark node not identical to dedicated infra but will give ballpark latency/throughput. i'll send results and scripts.
[06:15] Maya: ok, let's capture the POC acceptance criteria explicitly: 1) p95 latency <= 500ms for single-turn at steady load (45 QPS) and <=750ms during buffered bursts up to 180 QPS with accepted queuing under 2s; 2) quality parity defined by your eval set with no >5% regression on key metrics; 3) cost improvement target >=20% per 1k tokens or clear path to reach that with batching/quantization; 4) security/compliance checklist passed (SOC2 + KMS + audit logs implemented or plan documented).
[07:02] Laura: that's good. on the quality metric, we'll send the eval spreadsheet with pass/fail thresholds.
[07:08] Maya: perfect. timeline wrap-up  we need those artifacts from you: anonymized traffic CSV, top 50 prompts, eval spreadsheet, and network egress constraints. you'll get the questionnaire from me asap.
[07:20] Sanjay: will start questionnaire. one more Q: do you support retention controls on logs?
[07:25] Maya: yes, retention configurable; default hosted logs 7 days, can be disabled for private. we'll document audit log flows.
[07:32] Rita: for benchmark runs, any recommended tooling? we use k6 and some custom replay tooling.
[07:37] Diego: we have a JMeter and k6 script set, plus a replay harness that consumes your CSV. i'll share links.
[07:44] Maya: any other blockers?
[07:47] Laura: only legal review which might add a week. otherwise good.
[07:51] Maya: great. recap and next steps: send questionnaire, benchmark harness, schedule kickoff. we'll target to start integration week on 2026-03-31.
[07:59] Diego: i'll follow up with the initial benchmark scripts and an example replay CSV schema.
[08:04] Mike: i'll confirm peering details and egress limits by next monday.
[08:09] Sanjay: i'll run the security intake and come back with red flags.
[08:12] Maya: thanks all. we'll share the POC doc after this call.

Notes / Imperfections: transcription occasionally mislabels acronyms (e.g., K-V cash instead of KV cache, V-P-C for VPC), small filler words and crosstalk present. speaker labels mostly accurate but could be shifted in a few spots.
